# Implementing Trees: Defining Relationships

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Implementing Trees: Defining Relationships

Let's start by defining hierarchies from the root node. This node has three children.

![Adding the Three Children of Root](data:image/png;base64,)

Let's add this relationship using the add_child() method.

```cpp
root->add_child({child1, child2, child3});
```

### Defining Relationships of Leaf Nodes

i. Add children of child1.

![Adding Children of Node 1](data:image/png;base64,)

```cpp
child1->add_child({child1_1, child1_2, child1_3, child1_4});
```

ii. Add children of child2.

![Adding Children of Node 2](data:image/png;base64,)

```cpp
child2->add_child({child2_1});
```

iii. Add children of child3.

![Adding Children of Node 3](data:image/png;base64,)

```cpp
child3->add_child({child3_1, child3_2, child3_3});
```

### Creating the Tree

Now that we have created all the nodes and defined the hierarchy, we can finally create our tree.

```cpp
Tree<string> general_tree = Tree<string>(root);
```

Next, we will put all these codes together to create a fully functional tree.
